chapter: Brother Burnell and learning to read
title: Burnell imitating records
summary: Burnell copied whole recordings by Armstrong and Ellington on piano after hearing them once or twice.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Well, would you say his left hand was anything like Fat Swallow's left hand?
I'd say his hand was faster than Fat Swallow. He's right and left. Each one of them was just as fast as one of them.
But he would use that same style of left hand at these...

Well, he played different types of piano. In other words, he imitated very near anybody that he heard. He got a record of anyone. He listened at it. And after listening at the record once or twice, he set the piano and he'd be on there and play it like it.
I suppose he had a record of a full band. What could he do?

Yeah, at that time he would imitate... Lewis Armstrong was in full bloom with that mahogany hard stump and all that. Well, he played the mahogany hard stump just like Lewis played it on the record. Each man's part, he played it on the piano. If there was a bass solo in there, he played bass solo and saxophone solo and trumpet part. He played it just like the record was composed. That's the way he practiced playing. He'd take a record from Duke and play the record just like Duke made it.
